blocks.html: This documentation provides a reference to the `assignRolesWorkflow`. It belongs to the `@medusajs/medusa/core-flows` package.

This workflow assigns roles to reference entities (e.g. users, invites, or
custom entities). Each input assignment becomes one `rbac_role_assignment`
row, so a single run can assign different roles to different references,
each optionally constrained to its own scope.

It validates that the roles exist, that each reference is a grantee entity
configured for some actor type, and that the granting actor holds all the
policies of the roles being assigned.

steps.name: validateRolesExistStep
steps.description:
This step validates that the provided role IDs exist in the RBAC module.
Throws an error if any role is not found.

steps.name: validateAssignmentReferencesStep
steps.description:
This step validates that every reference is a grantee entity configured for
some actor type. An assignment to any other reference would never apply.

steps.name: validateActorRolePermissionsStep
steps.description:
Validates that the actor can grant every role being assigned or unassigned,
as decided by `canActorGrantRoles`: an actor can only assign roles whose
policies they themselves have, within the scope the assignment targets.

steps.name: createRoleAssignmentsStep
steps.description: This step creates one or more RBAC role assignments.

children.name: scope
children.description:
Optional scope constraint stored on the assignment: the role only applies
when acting within the given scope entity.

children.name: granting_scope
children.description:
The scope the granting actor is acting within. Their role assignments
scoped to it only allow assigning roles scoped to that same scope; assigning
roles to other scopes, or unscoped, requires their unscoped privileges.
